sections.kicker: Prepared for Wild Ink by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your Instagram the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: Wild Ink tells clients to say who they are for. Its own bio does not.
sections.keep: The visual world. Ornament, a deep maroon and cobalt, and a script wordmark that look the same on packaging, posts and logo.

sections.label: Front door
title: Three things people
meet first.
Three things

pins.what: The bio lists three disciplines and no client.
pins.why: Brand design and illustration is what thousands of studios write. It does not say who Wild Ink is for.
pins.how: Name the kind of founder or product this studio is best for.
pins.label: Your bio
pins.cost: Prospects hear a service list when they want a reason.

pins.quote: What makes you different and why people would choose you over competition.
pins.what: Your own checklist sets a standard your profile does not meet.
pins.why: Wild Ink says to know who you are for and what makes you different. The bio does neither.
pins.how: Apply the same checklist to the studio and publish the answer.
pins.label: Your voice
pins.cost: The advice sounds right and the proof is missing.

pins.area: Maroon, cobalt and ornamental patterns on the logo, packaging and posts
pins.what: Ornament, maroon and cobalt repeat across logo, pack and post.
pins.why: The look is distinct and recognisable in a feed of minimal studios.
pins.how: Name it as the studio's signature and lead the highlights with it.
pins.label: Your grid
pins.cost: A strong signature stays unlabelled and looks like taste instead of a method.

sections.intro: You asked for a look at Wild Ink. I spent some time on your Instagram. Three things stood out, and all three point the same way.
